## History

__Since before the time of Aristotle\, the stars and planets have been thought to be governed by geometric laws__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_1.png)

__Aristotle and Ptolemy both suggested that Earth was at the center of the universe and that all objects moved around it in uniform circular motion__

__The circle was a mystical and perfect structure to the ancients\, and they projected these ideas onto the heavens__

__It was thought that invisible crystalline spheres carried the planets and all other objects in space around the Earth in perfect circular motion__

__The ancients believed that there were four fundamental elements on Earth: air\, water\, fire and Earth\, and that a fifth\, the Quintessence or “ether” was perfect and incorruptible and held all things together__

__Aristotle’s solar system was __  __teleological__  __\, emphasizing perfect order and purpose in the natural world__

This is a Greek word meaning the opposite of  _chaos_ ;

The order or harmony of nature

__Importantly\, it was not based on empirical observation\, but philosophical premises emphasizing __  _cosmos _  __in the universe__

## Newton

__Besides developing the the Laws of Motion on Earth\, Isaac Newton examined the motion of the planets and Luna__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_2.png)

__Since falling objects accelerate\, they must have a force exerted on them__

__Whenever a force is exerted __  _on _  __an object\, it was exerted __  _by _  __some other object__

__According to legend\, Newton observed an apple falling from the top of a tree and was apparently struck with a moment of realization__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_3.png)

__If gravity works at the tops of trees\, or even the tops of mountains\, perhaps it acts all the way to the Moon__

__He did not have a satisfactory way of explaining how Earth could attract objects without touching them\, and many scientists initially rejected his “__  _spooky action at a distance_  __”__

## A New Center

__Copernicus\, Galileo\, Kepler\, and others had been measuring the positions of astronomical objects\, particularly the moon__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_4.png)

__It was discovered that the Moon kept an almost perfectly circular orbit around the Earth__

__Newton set about calculating the force of attraction that would keep Luna in uniform circular motion__

## An Inverse Square Law

__Newton discovered the gravity seems to obey an inverse square law: that is\, its magnitude decreases proportionally to the square of the distance between two objects:__

It turns out that this kind of relationship governs many things in nature

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_5.png)

__Using the latest observational values for the period of the Moon\, he was able to compute the \(average\) distance between Luna and Earth__

## A New Center

This is the acceleration of Earth on Luna\, not gravity when you stand on Luna

__Luna is approximately 60 Earth radii away\, so it feels a gravitational force of __

__ or the force of gravity here on Earth’s surface \(0\.00272 m/s__  __2__  __\)__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_6.png)

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_7.png)

__According to his own third law of motion\, the moon must also exert an equal and opposite force on the Earth__

## The symmetry of the Newton’s third law

__Thus\, the symmetry of those forces must be proportional to both masses\, leading to:__

The gravitational force between to objects is:

__directly__  proportional to the product of the masses and

__inversely__  proportional to the square of the distance between them

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_8.png)

__Newton’s math failed to explain the motion of the planets around the Earth\, but worked beautifully to explain Kepler and Brahe’s measurements in a heliocentric model__

## A magnum opus

__Newton’s pivotal mathematical description is now called the __  __Law of Universal Gravitation__  __\, and is written as:__

__Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them\. __

__This force always acts along a line joining the two particles\. __

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_9.png)

## The Law of Universal Gravitation

__Newton’s pivotal mathematical description is now called the __  __Law of Universal Gravitation__  __\, and is written mathematically as:__

We would have to wait another century to figure out the value of this constant of proportionality\, G

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_10.png)

It would be wise to store this as a variable in your calculator

This unit just makes the maths work out so the final computation produces a force in Newtons

__The value of__  _ _  __G was determined by Henry Cavendish in 1798 through an ingenious and relatively simply experiment involving __  __wire tension\, mirrors\, and light__

## Forever falling, forever missing the ground

__Satellites are put into orbit by accelerating them to sufficiently high tangential speeds__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_14.png)

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_15.png)

__If the speed is too low\, the Earth’s gravity will de\-orbit the satellite__

__If the speed is too high\, Earth’s gravity will be insufficient to hold it and it will escape __

## “Weightlessness” in orbit

__People and objects orbiting Earth are said to experience __  _apparent _  __weightlessness__  __\.__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_18.png)

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_19.png)

__This feels true to the person\, but it is only true __  __from their own frame of reference__

When the elevator is at rest\, the normal force balances out the weight of the person

When the elevator falls\, the person and elevator accelerate downward at equal rates

__At rest:__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_20.png)

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_21.png)

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_22.png)

__While falling:__

![](img%5C0%20Lecture%20_%2052%20Gravitation_23.png)

__But the acceleration of all objects \(elevator\, bag\, person\) is the same so relative to one another they do not __  _appear _  __to accelerate__

Mind what planet \(parent\) body you are working with

__Gravity is still acting on all objects and is still equal to ma__  __g__

__At sufficient distances from Earth \(or another source of gravity\)\, astronauts and spacecraft could experience “__  __true__  __ __  __weightlessness__  __”\, the absence of a \(significant\) gravitational force in any direction__

## Example 1 - An attractive date

Two humans\, one with mass 50 kg and another with mass 70 kg are sitting on a bench 0\.5 m apart from each other\.



  * __Calculate the attractive force of gravity between their two masses__
  * __Show that the unit of the Gravitational Constant\, __  _G_  __ yields an answer in Newtons__
  * __Determine the coefficient of friction required for the 50 kg person to begin sliding toward his/her amorous partner__
---

Giancoli pp. 120
9 x 10-7
Kg2 and m2 cancel; N remains
2 x 10-9 

~ 4900 N

## Example 4 | Geosynchronous Satellite

A  _geosynchronous_  satellite is one that stays above the same spot on Earth due to having an orbital period of 24 hours \(Earth’s rotational period\)\. Assume the satellite moves in a nearly perfectly circular orbit\.



  * __Determine the altitude \(height above surface\) that such a satellite must maintain__
  * __Determine the speed of the satellite__
  * __Compare this speed to one orbiting at 200 km above Earth__
---

Giancoli pp. 123

(a) 3.6 x 107 m (3.6 x 104 km)
(b) 3.0 x 103 m/s
(c ) ~8 x 103 m/s
